newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close nearly unchanged.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed nearly unchanged on Wednesday in quiet trading with mixed trading in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 to 104.93

"Unlinked bonds traded stable with a slightly positive trend," said Ronen Elgali, financial advisor at United Mizrahi Bank. "This because inflation expectations for the coming months are low, despite the expected high April consumer price index (CPI)."
April's CPI, which will be published on May 15, is generally high due to the Passover holiday. Forecasts are that it will be between 1.0-1.2 percent.

Elgali said trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a correction in some of the yields. "There is much uncertainty about what (the central bank's) interest rate policy will be with fears that interest rates won't go down."
Prices of the dollar-linked bonds were lower, he said, because of a weakening of the dollar in the world.
"There was demand for medium and long-term CPI-linked bonds with prices rising slightly," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
"All in all there was demand both for unlinked bonds and CPI-linked bonds which indicates there is some balance between the bonds," he said.
"Traders are waiting for April's CPI to be published, but don't expect surprises," the trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
